blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-performance-1 (One customer query per invoice in the monthly report) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: N+1 queries: `monthly_report` runs `invoices_of_month` once, then `customer_label` (`src/report.rs:39`, `db.customer(invoice.customer_id)?`) runs `SELECT id, name, country FROM customers WHERE id = $1` once per invoice — about 3 000 round trips for a month of finance's data (proposal: 3 000 invoices from 800 customers), growing linearly with the month's invoices, and fetching the same customer many times. The `Db` trait already offers the batch `customers(&self, ids: &[i64])` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`): collect the distinct `customer_id`s, call `db.customers(&ids)` once, build a `HashMap<i64, Customer>`, and look each invoice's customer up in it. Keep the invoice-number order and return the same error as today when a customer is missing.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

fn purchase_order(notes: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let pattern = Regex::new(r"PO-\d{4}-\d{4}").expect("a valid pattern");
findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called once per invoice from the loop at `src/report.rs:28`, and each call compiles `PO-\d{4}-\d{4}` anew — a pattern compilation per item (about 3 000 per monthly report), far costlier than the match itself. Compile it once, in a `static PATTERN: std::sync::LazyLock<Regex>` (or `OnceLock`), or compile it in `monthly_report` before the loop and pass it in.
findings.title: Regex compiled again for every invoice
